summary: Interrogated docs/specs/legacy-upgrade.md against decisions 0009 (frozen gate surface), 0016 (machinery dir rename), 0002 (one story per branch) and the mixed-ownership contract stated in upgrade.py. Two blocking findings, both resolved into the spec text.
gaps: The spec said the base commit for a legacy stage is 'recorded' without saying where it comes from. A base is what decides which commits count as the story's work; inferring it from branch topology would make that decision silently, and agentstats has no remote from which a default branch could even be probed.
contradictions: The spec said the .agents/ tree 'is removed' — a wholesale delete written into the same file that promises never to delete client additions (upgrade.py:29) and enforced nowhere. A client repo that placed its own content under .agents/ would lose it with no refusal and no report.
resolutions: Behaviour section rewritten: the legacy tree is retired by carry-then-verify. Skill-evolution dirs and client-added skills move from .agents/skills/ into factory/skills/ under the existing mixed-ownership rule; the remainder is deleted ONLY if every file left has a counterpart path in the newly vendored factory/ tree. Any unrecognized path aborts the upgrade and is named. Added as an acceptance criterion.

Behaviour section rewritten: `forge stage migrate --base <sha>` takes the base explicitly and validates that it resolves and is an ancestor of HEAD. Rationale recorded in the spec: migration is already a one-time act gated on --confirm-workspace-state, so the base belongs to the same human inspection. Acceptance criterion updated to name the flag and both refusals.
open_items: Non-blocking: archived evidence under .factory/history/ keeps its .agents/ paths and is excluded from the stale-reference report. Decision 0016 already designates itself the read-key for historical artifacts, so this is a restatement, not new scope.
Non-blocking: legacy prose verify_commands and opaque required_tests are not auto-converted. `forge doctor` already reports them (shipped in FORGE-DELEG-1) and the human re-records the decomposition.
